summary: Page Municipal Airport (PGA) is a public-use airport in the small city of Page, Arizona, situated near the Utah border in the heart of the Colorado Plateau. The airport primarily serves tourists visiting iconic nearby destinations including Lake Powell, Glen Canyon National Recreation Area, Horseshoe Bend, and Antelope Canyon. The city of Page itself was developed in the 1950s to support construction of the Glen Canyon Dam, giving the area a relatively young and tourism-focused character.
faqs:
Q: What major attractions are accessible from Page Municipal Airport?
A: The airport provides convenient access to Lake Powell, Glen Canyon National Recreation Area, Antelope Canyon, Horseshoe Bend, and the North Rim of the Grand Canyon, all within roughly 1-2 hours of driving time.

Q: Does Page Municipal Airport offer commercial service?
A: PGA is primarily a general aviation facility with limited commercial/charter operations; most scheduled airline service to the region uses larger airports such as Phoenix or Las Vegas.

Q: How far is the airport from Lake Powell?
A: The airport is located just a few miles from Lake Powell and Glen Canyon Dam, typically a short 10-15 minute drive to the marina area.

Q: Are there car rental services at the airport?
A: Rental car availability is limited at PGA itself, so visitors often arrange vehicles in advance or use shuttle services from larger nearby airports.
transport_tips: Rental cars are limited at the airport, so booking transportation in advance is advisable. Many visitors arrange round-trip shuttle services or guided tours from Page, especially for Antelope Canyon and Lake Powell excursions. The airport is a short drive from downtown Page and most lodging options along Lake Powell Boulevard.
local_tip: If you're flying in for a photography trip, plan your arrival for late morning—the soft afternoon light over Lake Powell and Horseshoe Bend is best captured a few hours after you land, giving you time to pick up supplies and check into accommodation before heading to the viewpoints.
